extracted.intended_audience: general NPR listeners and news readers
extracted.subtask_description: An NPR Morning Edition transcript reporting on Newsweek's apology for a disputed story about Quran desecration at Guantanamo, including discussion of sourcing, attribution, consequences, and the magazine's response. The page explains what went wrong in the reporting and how the editor described the errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize and acknowledge reporting errors when harm occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsweek apologizes to victims of deadly protests in Afghanistan and acknowledges reporting errors in a May 9 report that U.S. interrogators at Guantanamo Bay desecrated the Quran.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor issued an apology to those harmed and acknowledged that the magazine 'may have gotten certain things wrong.' The article frames apology as an appropriate response when reporting contributes to violence or harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate an acknowledgment from a retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not a retraction. It is an acknowledgement that we may have gotten certain things wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether a correction constitutes a retraction or a clarification/acknowledgment so readers understand what is being withdrawn or corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present a single source as multiple confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources, that should not have been the story. It was one source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate attribution must reflect the number and independence of sources; treating one source as multiple confirmations misleads readers and weakens credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overreliance on unnamed sources without corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters Michael Isikoff and John Barry cited unnamed sources in their brief item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using unnamed or anonymous sources, ensure sufficient corroboration and clearly communicate limits of attribution; unnamed sourcing in sensitive allegations requires extra verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm documentary evidence and solidify source recollection before reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Isikoff's source now doesn't recall precisely which documents he saw, but he still says he saw them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that sources can identify specific documents or evidence and confirm existence/contents of those documents before including such claims in a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat lack of objection as confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: A senior Defense Department official contradicted Newsweek's reporting elsewhere, but didn't object to the reference to the Koran. Newsweek took that as a second confirmation. But it wasn't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silence or non-objection from an official should not be used as confirmation; seek explicit, independent confirmation instead of inferring assent from silence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and consider potential consequences of reporting sensitive allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: That story led to deadly rioting in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should weigh the possible real-world impact of publishing sensitive allegations—especially in volatile contexts—and take extra care to verify and contextualize claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about what is known and what is not
rubrics_metrics.description: He's trying to be as clear as possible about what his magazine knows and what it doesn't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear to readers the limits of the publication's knowledge, indicate uncertainties, and avoid overstating confidence in unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue vigorous reporting to establish the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitaker says his staff will continue to report vigorously to learn the truth behind the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acknowledging errors or unresolved claims, newsrooms should pursue further reporting to establish facts and correct the record where necessary.
